ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Viet Nam's domestic terrorist/AML blacklist issued by the State Bank of Viet Nam, and PEP databases (World-Check or equivalent), with enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions and politically exposed persons; ongoing transaction monitoring under Decision No. 14/2022/QH14 and Circular No. 11/2023/TT-NHNN.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Registration Information System (NERIS) via the National Business Registration Portal (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be in Vietnamese script; Latin alphabet and Roman numerals permitted subject to readability and non-confusion; names must avoid being identical or confusingly similar to existing registered enterprises; must not violate historical, cultural, or national security interests; only words permissible under Article 38 of the Enterprise Law and Decree 01/2021/ND-CP; foreign-invested company may include transliterated forms in Vietnamese; cannot contain proper names only unless approved, and no prohibited tokens; Vietnamese diacritics are part of transliteration doctrine; a name in Latin script may be used concurrently but the Vietnamese-language legal name is controlling; foreign words may be included only if compliant with written Vietnamese structure and not misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: National name or flag-derived terms (e.g., 'Viet Nam', 'Socialist Republic of Viet Nam', 'Quốc hội', 'Chính phủ', 'Cộng hòa xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam')
Armed forces names (e.g., 'Quân đội Nhân dân', 'Công an Nhân dân')
State-owned special entities and administrative organs names (e.g., 'Bộ', 'Tỉnh', 'Thành phố' in ways implying state affiliation)
Words implying royal, religious, or official endorsement without prior ministerial approval (e.g., 'Hoàng gia', 'Vua', 'Giáo', 'Thanh tra')
Terms requiring sectoral licensing or ministerial approval (e.g., 'Ngân hàng', 'Bảo hiểm', 'Chứng khoán', 'Báo', 'Tạp chí', 'Xuất khẩu lao động', 'Môi giới việc làm')
Obscene, violent, or anti-social terms contrary to national traditions and ethics
Terms identical or confusingly similar to existing protected trade names
Foreign words that are not expressed in Vietnamese script in a way consistent with Vietnamese phonetics
Abbreviations or acronyms that are misleading about the nature of business
'Global EOR' or 'Staffing Agency' in English-only format without Vietnamese transliteration if unsupported by a license
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written complaint/appeal to the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) that issued the registration decision, requesting a review under the Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13; the DPI decision can be appealed administratively to the provincial People's Committee, and ultimately a court action may be filed under Law on Administrative Procedures No. 93/2015/QH13; time-bar: administrative appeal within 90 days of the notice, court complaint within 30 days of administrative appeal decision; with online filing extension available via NERIS; resubmit corporation name or select an alternative name during the 30-day reservation; re-validation may be obtained for unexpired mutual consent of the applicant, but a new reservation is generally required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permitted as a registered address for a foreign-invested LLC; the registered address must be a physical land/building address in Viet Nam held under lease, ownership, or legal usage right; however, teleworking and remote HR activities may be performed outside, but the registered office must host statutory records and be accessible for inspection; virtual office may serve only as a business support office and cannot be the registered address for enterprise registration; the industry of labor leasing/EOR requires a physical operational center for payroll administration and labor contract records; home-based offices may be accepted in narrow residential purposes, but not recommended for EOR staffing due to licensing and labor levy requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High (estimated 65% probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection within first 12 months of operation due to labor-export/recruitment licensing, AML/CFT supervision, and tax file audits by the DPI, State Inspectorate, and labor authorities)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises of Viet Nam No. 59/2020/QH14 (Articles 25–27 on incorporation, Article 28 on legal representative, Article 49 on capital contribution deadline, Articles 74–76 on limited liability companies); Law on Investment of Viet Nam No. 61/2020/QH14 (Articles 36–39 on foreign investment registration and market access); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Business Registration (Articles 12–33); Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP on Implementation of the Law on Investment; Decree No. 23/2021/ND-CP on Employment Services (industry licensing condition).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province where the head office is located, through its Business Registration Office and one-stop administrative division; online filing is conducted through the National Enterprise Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp) as prescribed under Article 25 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, accompanied by the company Charter, list of members, capital contribution schedule, and statutory attachments; for a foreign-invested LLC the dossier is filed after the issuance of the Investment Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Law on Enterprises 2020 does not impose a general minimum charter capital for a service LLC; however, because the EOR/staffing scope constitutes an employment service under Decree No. 23/2021/ND-CP, the enterprise must demonstrate a charter capital of at least VND 1,000,000,000 (approx. USD 41,000) and maintain a statutory security deposit of at least VND 500,000,000 (approx. USD 20,500) at a licensed Vietnamese commercial bank. Subscribed capital must be contributed in full within 90 days after the Enterprise Registration Certificate is granted, through each member's remittance to the company's dedicated capital contribution account at a licensed Vietnamese bank, with bank statements forming the capital-contribution evidence under Article 49 of the Law on Enterprises 2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF MEMBERS / OWNER'S WRITTEN RESOLUTION NO. 01/2025 OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (VN_LLC) — ADOPTED AT [HEAD OFFICE ADDRESS], VIET NAM, THIS [DATE]. THE MEMBERS, UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Company's charter capital is fixed at VND 1,000,000,000 (one billion Vietnamese dong). The subscribed capital attributable to each member is set out in the Annex to this resolution; each member shall contribute its subscribed capital in full within 90 days from the Enterprise Registration Certificate date by wire transfer into the Company's dedicated capital contribution account at a licensed Vietnamese commercial bank, and the bank deposit slips shall be retained as statutory evidence. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered head office of the Company is hereby adopted at [full street address, ward, district, province], Viet Nam, for all corporate, tax, and service-licensing purposes; the lease agreement and lawful title documents of the lessor shall be kept in the Company's statutory dossier, and any subsequent relocation shall be effective only upon a further members' resolution and notification to the Business Registration Office. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The members hereby appoint Mr./Ms. [full name], holder of identification document [number], as Chairman of the Company and as General Director, and such General Director is designated the sole legal representative of the Company pursuant to Article 28 of the Law on Enterprises 2020, with full authority to execute all administrative, tax, banking, labor, and licensing instruments on behalf of the Company. 4. IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZATION: The Chairman and the General Director are jointly and severally authorized to open corporate settlement and payroll accounts; to sign the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate applications; to file all tax, seal, publication, and statistical declarations; to apply for the employment services license under Decree No. 23/2021/ND-CP; to engage external legal counsel; and to execute all occupancy, fire-safety, environmental registration, and occupational-safety clearance documents. 5. ENTRY INTO FORCE: This resolution takes full effect upon its date of signature and supersedes any prior consents. EXECUTED THIS [DATE] AT [LOCATION]. (ANNEX: LIST OF MEMBERS AND SUBSCRIBED CAPITAL PERCENTAGES; NOTARIZED SIGNATURE SPECIMENS.)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (Tong Cuc Thue) under the Ministry of Finance of Viet Nam; online portal: https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn (National E-Tax Portal)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a foreign-invested limited liability company through the National Enterprise Registration Portal (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) or at the provincial Department of Planning and Investment to obtain an Enterprise Registration Certificate containing the preliminary tax identification number. Step 2: Activate the tax identity via the E-Tax Portal using the preliminary tax code, submit initial tax registration form (Form 05/DK-THGT), and obtain the definitive TIN. Step 3: Register the VAT calculation method (standard credit method), appoint a legal representative as the electronic transaction contact, and register an electronic tax invoice account with a digital signature certificate issued by an approved certificate authority. Step 4: Complete e-tax declaration registration and electronic invoice issuance authorization. Step 5: For foreign contractors without a domestic entity, the payer must register a Foreign Contractor Tax withholding account using Forms 02/GTGT or 05/GTGT on behalf of the non-resident before the first payment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income, with foreign tax credit relief; non-resident shareholders taxed at entity level; Export Processing Enterprises (EPEs) located in export processing zones enjoy territorial exemption on indirect taxes, but the LLC remains a fully taxable resident legal entity for corporate income tax
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Vietnamese tax law; the LLC is mandatorily classified as a taxable resident enterprise. Available statutory elections include: (i) election between the VAT credit method and the direct/gross-receipt method for eligible taxpayers, (ii) election by a foreign contractor to apply the Foreign Contractor Tax deduction method instead of the direct method (subject to conditions), (iii) election to file consolidated VAT returns with dependent branches, and (iv) election under domestic hybrid mismatch alignment rules (Decree 132/2020/ND-CP) to ensure deduction and timing consistency with the counterparty jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax, known as Thue Gia Tri Gia Tang)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary VAT registration threshold for limited liability companies; all businesses with declared revenue must register for VAT and file monthly or quarterly returns. Only households and individuals not organized as enterprises with annual revenue below VND 100,000,000 may remain outside the VAT net; the effective threshold for LLCs is VND 0 of registration relief.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing since 1 July 2022 under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Every e-invoice must contain a Tax Authority Invoice Code (ma so cua co quan thue) obtained in real time through the General Department of Taxation portal; XML invoice data is transmitted to the tax authority immediately at issuance with no physical stamping. For point-of-sale transactions, cash-register invoices with QR codes must be transmitted to the tax authority within 2 hours of the transaction. Real-time fiscal clearance uses an application-programming-interface (API) gateway and digital machine-readable stamping embedded in the invoice XML.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported goods and services supplied and consumed outside Viet Nam qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC and Decree 123/2020/ND-CP. For a Global EOR / staffing platform, the services must be supplied to a foreign organization or individual under a written contract, consumed entirely outside Viet Nam, and evidenced by payment received from abroad through a foreign-currency bank account. The taxpayer must maintain a complete service-performance file proving the offshore consumption and absence of domestic use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form HQ/2015/XK) bearing the electronic customs clearance barcode
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the physical export route (for physical exports)
Commercial Invoice issued in the name of the Vietnamese LLC
Export Sales Contract or Service Agreement signed with the foreign counterparty
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank confirmation of foreign-currency wire transfer proving payment from abroad
Zero-rated e-invoice with Tax Authority Invoice Code
Packing List and Certificate of Origin (for physical goods) or Service Performance Certificate and detailed work log (for offshore services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims are reassessed retrospectively with full VAT at 10%, plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the unpaid amount, and administrative fines ranging from 1 to 3 times the evaded tax (theoretical cap of 3 times). Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline triggers foreign-exchange administrative penalties of up to 10% of the outstanding amount. Criminal liability may attach under Penal Code No. 100/2015/QH13 (Article 200) for tax evasion, with fines up to VND 4,500,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 20 years. Tax-exemption or zero-rating benefits may be clawed back for up to 10 years from the date of the fraudulent claim, and the taxpayer may be placed on the GDT high-risk audit watchlist.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), the sole apex authority for foreign exchange administration, derives its mandate from the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam No. 46/2010/QH12 and the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11, as amended by Ordinance No. 05/2008/PL-UBTVQH12. The Ministry of Finance and the General Department of Taxation exercise supporting control over tax-clearance documentation required for cross-border profit repatriation; the licensing of banks, the operation of payment systems, and the authorization of all onshore foreign-exchange products rest exclusively with the SBV.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: VND operates under a conditionally convertible regime. Current-account transactions, which include the receipt of Global Employer of Record (EOR) management fees and payroll-processing fees by the Vietnamese LLC from overseas clients, are convertible and freely transferable provided the underlying service agreements, invoices, bank receipts, and commercial documentation are maintained; no investment license approval is required for inward service revenue. Capital-account transactions, including shareholder capital contributions, intra-group loans, and equity increases, require a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a licensed commercial bank under Circular No. 06/2019/TT-NHNN. Dividend and after-tax profit remittances are treated as capital-account transfers and are permitted only at year-end, after the annual audited financial statements are issued, the corporate income tax (CIT) finalization is completed, and the local tax authority confirms that no tax obligations remain outstanding; the remittance is executed through the DICA in tranches matching the finalized tax year. A pure offshore treasury model, in which service revenues are collected outside Vietnam via a non-licensed digital payment provider and local payroll is funded by informal remittance, is not permissible under SBV exchange-control law and would constitute unauthorized foreign-exchange activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vietnam does not impose general mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds for cross-border services. Under the amended foreign-exchange ordinance, specific mandatory-surrender obligations are limited to particular commodity groups such as crude oil and strategic minerals, with ratios set administratively by the SBV; these rules do not apply to an ISIC 7810 employment and staffing entity. The statutory obligation for the EOR company is to repatriate all service export receivables into a licensed foreign-currency account or the DICA held at an SBV-licensed credit institution, retaining the underlying contract, invoice, and non-cash settlement records for at least five years. Market practice and prudent bank risk policy require repatriation within 30 calendar days of the invoice due date; a materially longer lag without a documented bilateral payment plan will be treated by the bank as a suspicious disguised borrowing and will trigger enhanced AML review. There is no mandatory VND conversion ratio for service export receipts under the current framework.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rated Low-Medium as a complementary rail only. Offshore digital EMIs and cross-border payment platforms, including Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Mercury, and similar providers, are not licensed to open or maintain local Vietnamese payment accounts for a resident corporate entity under Decree No. 101/2012/ND-CP on non-cash payments, as amended by Decree No. 70/2019/ND-CP, and Circular No. 39/2014/TT-NHNN on intermediary payment services. They cannot serve as the primary treasury or clearing vehicle for a Vietnamese LLC, cannot legally receive EOR revenue as a substitute for the DICA, and cannot disburse VND payroll to local employees. Lawful deployment is limited to the outbound payout function: the Vietnamese LLC may instruct its licensed onshore bank to convert USD/EUR surplus and fund a Wise or equivalent business account for disbursement of wages to overseas independent contractors residing outside Vietnam, provided the contractor agreements, tax declarations, and sanctions-screening records are retained. Use of a foreign EMI as the main inbound collection account would be classified as unauthorized intermediary payment service and a breach of SBV exchange-control regulations, exposing the entity to administrative sanctions and potential criminal liability under the Penal Code. The recommended architecture is a licensed local bank as the primary spine, with an EMI serving purely as an ancillary offshore contractor payout engine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the locally appointed legal representative of a foreign-invested LLC at the initial corporate account opening. Vietnamese banks are digitizing e-KYC for natural persons, but corporate DICA and foreign-currency account opening still requires an in-branch interview with the statutory legal representative or a board-authorized local signatory who produces original corporate seals, IRC, business registration certificate, and articles of association. Non-resident beneficial owners and foreign directors may execute notarized powers of attorney and deliver certified passport copies and board resolutions, but a fully remote account opening without any physical appearance in Vietnam is not currently recognized by tier-1 banks. Video-conference KYC may supplement but does not replace the first in-person meeting. For a foreign-owned LLC operating an EOR platform, the bank will also require the valid employment-services license issued by the provincial Department of Labor, Invalids and Social Affairs (DOLISA), and the physical presence of the local director materially accelerates the onboarding timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) structure anchored in an offshore financial center or high-risk jurisdiction without a clear commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate ownership chart from the Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) through every intermediate entity to the ultimate individual shareholder; certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for each offshore entity; passport copies, PEP declarations, and sanctions-list attestation for each UBO; sponsor bank reference letters from the remitting institution; and audited group financial statements evidencing the operational reality of the parent group.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Business Registration Office under the Ministry of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 30 for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from VND 1,000,000 to VND 15,000,000; continued non-filing may trigger enforcement actions and potential administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (via the National Investment Information System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 30 for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission penalties under Investment Law; repeated failure may result in administrative sanctions and limited extension of investment registration certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Tax Department under the General Department of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 0.03% per day on overdue amounts; penalties for late filing and under-declaration; enforced collection and tax code freezing for serious non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements submitted with Annual Tax Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department and the Department of Planning and Investment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the final CIT return deadline; audited statements must accompany the filing for foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties for failure to attach audited statements; tax assessment may be rejected; repeated violations may lead to audit rectification orders and suspension of operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) in Vietnam, including foreign-owned limited liability companies, are subject to a mandatory annual independent audit regardless of revenue or asset size. Other enterprises are exempt only if they do not meet statutory thresholds for total assets, revenue, or employment and do not qualify as public companies or regulated financial institutions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) and statutory charts of accounts for legal-entity financial statements; IFRS may be adopted for consolidated reporting when required by the foreign parent group and approved by the competent authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual enterprise report requires confirmation that the member/register data, shareholding structure, and ultimate beneficial owners are current and accurate. Any transfer of capital contributions or changes in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the corporate registers and notified to the business registration authority within 10 days of the transaction. No separate standalone UBO annual filing exists under current law.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100 - 300 USD per year for a professional registered agent and legal address service in Vietnam
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,200 - 4,500 USD per year for a small/medium global EOR staffing agency

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% standard CIT rate for all resident companies under Vietnam's Law on Corporate Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12, as amended by Law No. 32/2013/QH13.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard global employer-of-record and cross-border payroll services are not eligible for sector-specific CIT holidays and therefore bear the 20% headline rate. Eligible projects in high-technology zones, software production, high-tech ancillary industries, education, healthcare, and similar encouraged sectors can access a reduced CIT rate of 10% for up to 15 years, frequently combined with a 4-year full CIT exemption and a 9-year 50% reduction. Research and development expenditures may also be deductible at 150% of actual cost within the clean-environment and high-technology incentive framework. Export processing enterprise status mainly grants import duty and VAT facilitation, not an automatic CIT rate reduction. Any incentive claim must be substantiated with an incentive annexure attached to the annual CIT finalisation return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02/TNDN, the quarterly provisional corporate income tax return filed through the General Department of Taxation e-portal at etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn; electronic filing is mandatory for all registered enterprises.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter: Q1 by 30 April, Q2 by 30 July, Q3 by 30 October, Q4 by 30 January of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise name, Vietnamese tax code, registered address, ISIC business code, and fiscal year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign-invested LLC must use its own Vietnamese tax identification number; the offshore parent company must not be substituted as the taxpayer. Data should be pre-populated from the eTax entity profile and corrected before submission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated quarterly taxable income computed on cumulative year-to-date revenue from global EOR service fees, retainer fees, setup fees, payroll administration fees, and consultancy charges minus documented arm's length deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Vietnam-source and foreign-source income must be separable in the accounting records. Salary advances and payroll-disbursed remuneration should be presented as payroll-related cash flows, with the service fee clearly identified as taxable business revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable equals provisional taxable income multiplied by 20% or by any applicable preferential CIT rate. The cumulative quarterly prepayment must be reasonably estimated to avoid the statutory under-payment sanction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A DTA does not reduce the Vietnamese LLC's entity-level CIT on its own profits; treaty relief applies, where valid, only to cross-border withholding taxes on interest and royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing beyond 30 days carries fines up to VND 25,000,000 per return; underpayment of provisional quarterly tax attracts default interest at 0.03% per day. Under-declared taxable income, when ultimately assessed at finalisation, attracts a 20% supplementary penalty on the deficient tax under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 03/TNDN, the annual corporate income tax finalisation return submitted through etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn together with audited financial statements, related-party transaction disclosure schedules, tax incentive schedules, and transfer pricing documentation where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 90 days from the end of the fiscal year; for a 31 December year-end, the finalisation dossier is due no later than 31 March of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item A - Revenue from business activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from global employer-of-record and cross-border contractor payroll services, including all administration fees, payroll processing fees, compliance fees, gross-up reimbursements, and other service charges, converted into VND at the transaction-date exchange rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC file is a full-tax-rate return on its assessable Vietnamese-source and treaty-allocated foreign-source income. If the EOR contract expressly separates payroll disbursements, statutory social contributions, and the service fee, the reimbursement side can be presented outside service revenue; otherwise the tax authority will treat the full amount as taxable turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Items B and C - Deductible expenses and other income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All valid and voucher-supported costs: Vietnamese employee salaries, statutory social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance, payroll software, office costs, professional indemnity insurance, legal fees, accounting fees, licensing fees, depreciation, and destination-management subcontractor costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility requires lawful e-invoices, actual bank payment traces, and correct allocation to revenue. Fees paid to the offshore parent for platform licences, administrative support, and global management services are deductible only if the Vietnamese entity can evidence actual receipt of services, arm's length pricing, and inclusion in a complete transfer pricing dossier.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Items D through G - Taxable income, CIT rate, incentives and final tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after the statutory 5-year loss carryforward; application of the 20% headline rate or a reduced incentive rate; computation of final CIT payable after the four quarterly prepayments; final balance due or overpayment refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Profit distribution to the offshore shareholder is not declared on this form. The finalisation return, audited financial statements, and paid CIT must be reconciled before the licensed remittance bank will accept a profit repatriation application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late finalisation by more than 30 days attracts a fine up to VND 25,000,000. Understated tax is subject to a 20% supplementary penalty on the under-declared amount, default interest of 0.03% per day, and, in aggravated cases, criminal tax evasion liability. Incorrect VAT treatment on payroll administration invoices is separately corrected and penalised.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% at source under Vietnam's entity-level CIT system. A Vietnamese LLC may distribute after-tax profits to a foreign corporate shareholder without an additional dividend withholding tax, provided the statutory profit remission documents are completed through a licensed Vietnamese bank.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because domestic law imposes no dividend withholding tax, no DTA relief is required for ordinary profit distribution; treaty benefits cannot be invoked to obtain refunds or new exemptions in respect of dividends. For cross-border interest and royalty payments, the foreign beneficial owner must present a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by its home tax authority to the Vietnamese payor before or at the time of payment, together with a Form 01/NTNN foreign contractor tax registration confirmation and a beneficial-owner declaration. The Vietnamese payor is the withholding agent and must apply the treaty rate only after the full dossier is accepted; the Principal Purpose Test under the OECD Multilateral Instrument and Vietnamese GAAR applies to all treaty claims.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic deemed withholding on cross-border debt interest is generally 5% CIT on gross interest, with no VAT payable. Royalties and intellectual-property licence fees are generally subject to deemed withholding of 10% CIT and 5% VAT on the gross royalty. Vietnam's DTA network typically caps interest withholding at 10% and royalties at 10%-15%; the lower of the domestic deemed rate and the applicable treaty cap applies after formal treaty benefit approval, with the cap denied if the recipient is not the beneficial owner or the arrangement is structured to defeat the purpose of the DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, compulsory Vietnamese transfer pricing documentation is triggered when the taxpayer's ordinary business revenue reaches VND 50 billion in a tax year and the aggregate value of related-party transactions reaches VND 30 billion in the same tax year. Even below these thresholds, documentation must be supplied immediately if the tax authority raises a TP audit query. The Master File is separately required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds approximately VND 18,000 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam has not enacted a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations regime; however, Decree 132/2020/ND-CP applies the OECD-aligned substance-over-form and anti-avoidance principles requiring the Vietnamese EOR entity to receive profits consistent with the functions it performs, the assets it owns, and the risks it assumes. The LLC must maintain a physical office, locally employed HR and payroll tax specialists, actual employment contracts, Vietnamese payroll and social insurance records, and independent decision-making files. A letterbox entity that merely issues invoices and passes profits to a foreign platform affiliate will be re-characterised, disregarded, or denied deductions for lacking economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Revenue Under-Reporting and False Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting EOR administration fees, payroll gross-ups, and cross-border service revenues from Vietnamese books; using offshore bank accounts or unregulated digital payroll rails to receive client fees without booking them; creating ghost employees, artificial payroll subcontractors, or fake e-invoices to inflate deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative assessment, 20% supplementary penalty on under-declared tax, and 0.03% daily interest under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP. Criminal tax evasion under Article 200 of the Penal Code applies where evaded tax is from VND 100 million; fines may reach VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment may reach up to 7 years in serious or repeat cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, chief accountant, and any director who signs false CIT returns are jointly and severally liable for undercollected tax. Veil piercing is applied for instances of intentional misconduct, resulting in personal fines, asset confiscation, temporary exit bans, and imprisonment of the responsible directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing the Vietnamese LLC as a pure invoicing shell between foreign clients and remote workers, with no Vietnamese personnel, no operational office, no payroll infrastructure, no local accounting records, and no employment-risk assumption; transferring all value to an offshore platform company while keeping no meaningful profit in Vietnam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard the entity or re-characterise its transactions, attribute the entire platform profit to Vietnam, disallow related-party deductions, impose the 20% CIT adjustment plus penalties and interest, and refer the entity for revocation by the licensing authority and the Department of Planning and Investment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who never exercise management functions cannot rely on the corporate veil. They are personally exposed to fines for false licensing declarations, administrative sanctioning, travel bans, disqualification from directorship, and criminal prosecution for intentional misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive intra-group platform licence fees, booking unreceipted management charges from the offshore parent, manipulating the Vietnamese EOR entity's routine margin below the arm's length return, imposing one-sided profit splits, or failing to prepare the mandatory TP Local File and Master File after crossing the VND 50 billion / VND 30 billion thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Department of Taxation will make a transfer-pricing adjustment, increase taxable income at the 20% CIT rate, apply a 20% penalty on the under-declared tax, charge 0.03% daily interest, and deny treaty relief under the Principal Purpose Test. The taxpayer is placed on the tax-authority risk blacklist and may be subjected to mandatory on-site TP inspections.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who choose, implement, and sign the intra-group pricing policy face personal liability for deficient TP documentation, withdrawal of treaty benefits, and collection from their personal assets where the pricing arrangement is found to be a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed EOR and Labour Supply Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an employer-of-record or labour-dispatch arrangement that assigns employees to third-party client sites in Vietnam without a valid labour-dispatch licence from the provincial Department of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs, while continuing to invoice clients for workforce services under ISIC 7810.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The labour authority may impose administrative fines, confiscate unlawful service fees, and order immediate suspension of the unlicensed payroll platform. The tax authority independently re-characterises the illegal activity as ordinary Vietnamese-source business income, denies deductions for expenses connected to unlicensed operations, and restates all CIT and VAT liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who signs labour-supply contracts without the required licence is personally fined, disqualified from managing employment-service companies, subject to travel bans, and criminally exposed if the arrangement facilitated undeclared foreign workers or social insurance evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Cross-Border Payment Infrastructure Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using personal bank accounts, unregulated digital wallets, Wise/PayPal remittance channels, or cash to process cross-border client fees and employee payroll in Vietnam; bypassing State Bank of Vietnam licensed payment institutions; failing to maintain beneficial-owner due diligence files; executing transfers in unrecognised tokens or through shell accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative financial penalties under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering and Decree 116/2023/ND-CP, closure of bank and digital payment channels, revocation of licences, and confiscation of illicit proceeds. If the underlying funds derive from criminal activity, money laundering under Article 324 of the Penal Code may result in imprisonment of up to 15 years and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors identified as beneficial owners of unlawful payroll flows face criminal investigation, personal confiscation, exit bans, disqualification from managing regulated financial and payment institutions, and imprisonment for knowingly executing or authorising the unlawful cross-border transfers.
